svg.text: HOW A CONDITION TRAVELS THROUGH A FAMILY
The pattern in the family tree tells you which kind of inheritance it is.

g.text: Needs TWO faulty copies to show
Carriers are healthy and unaware
Two carriers: 1 in 4 affected,
2 in 4 carriers, 1 in 4 clear
Sickle cell disease. Skips generations.
ONE faulty copy is enough
An affected parent, every pregnancy:
1 in 2 chance, boys and girls alike
No healthy carriers
Appears in every generation.

svg.text: X-LINKED RECESSIVE — WHY IT LOOKS LIKE A DISEASE OF BOYS

g.text: A boy has only one X. If it carries the fault there is no second copy to cover it, so he is affected.
A girl has two X chromosomes, so she is usually a healthy carrier.
A carrier mother: half her sons affected, half her daughters carriers. A father never passes it to his son.
Haemophilia and colour blindness follow this pattern. Look for affected uncles on the mother's side.

svg.text: A MUTATION IS NOT ALWAYS A DISEASE

g.text: Most change nothing. A few are harmful.
A few are useful: sickle TRAIT protects
against severe malaria.
Give the numbers and the options.
The couple chooses. Never tell them
whether to marry or to conceive.

svg.text: Every pregnancy carries the same risk. Having one affected child does not protect the next.
Families believe otherwise, and the belief causes real distress. Say it explicitly.
